name: Afamelanotide

lead: Afamelanotide, also called Melanotan I and sold as Scenesse, is a synthetic analogue of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone. It is delivered as a subcutaneous implant and is approved in the European Union and the United States for adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP), a rare inherited disorder in which sunlight causes severe pain.

It is discussed in looksmaxxing communities because it darkens skin, and it is sometimes described as the approved counterpart of gray-market Melanotan II. The strong evidence applies only to its approved medical use; it is a prescription product for a specific disease and is not approved as a cosmetic tanning product.

paras: Afamelanotide is a relatively selective agonist at the melanocortin-1 receptor on melanocytes. Stimulating MC1R increases production of eumelanin, the photoprotective brown-black pigment, and may also support DNA repair and antioxidant responses. In EPP the increased pigmentation and related effects allow patients to tolerate more light exposure before symptoms appear.

In clinical trials adverse events were generally mild, with headache, nausea and implant-site reactions most often reported; skin darkening and changes in existing moles are expected effects, so regular skin checks are advised. It is available only by prescription through specialist centres and is costly. Its safety data come from regulated clinical use and do not cover unregulated melanotan products.
